response.message:
Deciding between solo play and a multiplayer session usually comes down to a few personal factors. First, think about your mood: if you’re looking to unwind, reflect, or get lost in a story, a single‑player experience can be soothing and lets you set your own pace. If you crave social interaction, competition, or teamwork, playing with friends can add excitement and shared memories. 

Next, consider your schedule and energy level. Solo games let you play in short bursts or long stretches without coordinating with anyone else, while multiplayer often requires everyone to be available at the same time. Finally, reflect on what you want to get out of the session—whether it’s a narrative journey, a mental challenge, or a chance to laugh and bond with friends. We can explore options that fit whichever vibe you’re leaning toward when you’re ready.
